title: Inversion of Control via Custom State Reducer
concept: State Reducer Pattern & Middleware Action Interception
problemStatement: Implement `createReducibleStore(baseReducer, initialState, customReducer)` where state transitions run through `customReducer(state, action, defaultNextState)` before updating, allowing callers to override or prevent specific actions.
interviewTrap: The State Reducer pattern (popularized by Downshift) empowers library users to block specific internal actions (e.g. preventing a dropdown from closing on Enter) without forking the component.

testCases.name: Executes default reducer transitions normally
testCases.testFn: const base = (s, a) => a.type === 'INC' ? { count: s.count + 1 } : s; const store = createReducibleStore(base, { count: 0 }); store.dispatch({ type: 'INC' }); return store.getState();

testCases.name: User custom reducer intercepts and overrides specific actions
testCases.input: custom reducer blocks decrement below zero
testCases.testFn: const base = (s, a) => a.type === 'DEC' ? { count: s.count - 1 } : s; const custom = (s, a, next) => next.count < 0 ? s : next; const store = createReducibleStore(base, { count: 0 }, custom); store.dispatch({ type: 'DEC' }); return store.getState();

testCases.name: Preserves state identity when actions are blocked
testCases.input: verify state object reference equality when action is prevented
testCases.testFn: const base = (s) => ({ ...s }); const custom = (s) => s; const initial = { val: 1 }; const store = createReducibleStore(base, initial, custom); store.dispatch({ type: 'TEST' }); return store.getState() === initial;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: The State Reducer pattern allows the consumer of a custom hook to intercept and customize state transitions before they are committed, giving developers total control without modifying hook internals.
